invariants.text: Collaborative edits are gated by existing project permissions: only members with edit permission (or owner) may mutate shared content; view members are strictly read-only, both server-side (viewer inbound update/sync dropped in Room.handle_update) and client-side (canEdit gate).
invariants.home: WS handshake re-validates JWT (decode_access_token + email->User, mirroring get_current_user/deps.py) then require_project_editor(get_project_access(...)) resolving project_id via textBox.record.project_id; client gate via Project.current_user_permission/can_edit_content (domain.ts). All primitives exist in code.

invariants.text: The collaboration/document unit is a single record and its content blocks (Record 1-N TextBox); a shared session is scoped to exactly one record. (Status at-risk: implementation currently scopes a room per TextBox.id rather than per record.)
invariants.home: Deferred record-scoped session wrapper (one record Y.Doc whose block map hosts each block as a named Y.Text keyed on TextBox.id). Current increment builds room-per-TextBox.id, not per-record.

invariants.text: Every realtime connection authenticates with the same JWT/current-user identity used by REST (decode_access_token -> sub/email -> User), before joining a room; there is no unauthenticated realtime access.
PostgreSQL remains the durable system of record: relational Record/TextBox state stays consistent enough that existing REST reads, search, tags, and notifications keep functioning unchanged.

Content blocks retain stable identity (integer TextBox.id): CRDT edits never create/delete/re-key rows, so tag_textBox associations and mention/notification derivation keyed on a text box continue to resolve after concurrent edits.
invariants.home: apps/api/app/collab/rooms.py (Room/RoomRegistry keyed by integer TextBox.id) + apps/api/app/collab/routes.py:34 (/ws/text-boxes/{text_box_id:int}) + apps/api/app/collab/persistence.py:_persist (UPDATE-only write-back to the existing TextBox row)

invariants.text: textBox_content's length constraint must be respected or migrated: CRDT-materialised content can exceed the former String(1000) cap, so it is widened to TEXT (Alembic 20260421_0004), which also adds the textBox_crdt_state snapshot column.

Concurrent edits by multiple users to the same record converge to a single consistent state for all participants, with no lost updates and no manual conflict resolution (CRDT convergence). (Status at-risk: no CRDT engine wired; current path is last-writer-wins full-text overwrite.)
invariants.home: Server-authoritative pycrdt/y-py Y.Doc per room + Yjs sync step1/step2 + state-vector exchange on connect; client binds Y.Text to the editor for character-level merge.

invariants.text: Edits propagate to all currently-connected participants in near-real-time via WS relay broadcast within a text-box room, not only on explicit save or page reload.
invariants.home: In-process WS router under /api/v1 doing per-text-box-room relay broadcast on the existing uvicorn[standard] process (bundles the websockets stack); single node.

invariants.text: A client that goes offline and later reconnects merges its local offline changes with server/peer state without conflict, converging to the same state as if it had stayed connected. (Status at-risk: client re-sends buffered full text on reconnect, which clobbers rather than merges.)
invariants.home: Yjs sync handshake on WS connect (rooms.py, unbuilt) + snapshot rehydration (persistence.py / BYTEA, unbuilt)

invariants.text: Convergence is order-independent and idempotent: reordered or duplicated update delivery does not change the final converged state (CRDT commutativity/idempotency).
invariants.home: Per-textBox in-memory pycrdt Y.Doc + pycrdt-websocket YRoom relay (server applies each inbound update to room.ydoc and broadcasts). Named seam-1 (Peer A handle_update <-> Peer B handle_update, same Room) is clean by construction: a single uvicorn event loop serializes doc.apply_update, and Yjs/pycrdt update commutativity+idempotency+associativity (yjs-collab-guide.md §7) makes interleave/reorder/duplicate converge.

invariants.text: The relational TextBox representation eventually reflects the converged CRDT state (eventual consistency between shared document and Postgres materialization) via the debounced flush, so A4 holds after edits settle.
invariants.home: Debounced persist_snapshot flush: decode Y.Doc -> set textBox_content on ORM instance -> commit (fires updated_at onupdate)

revisions.change:
Fork "SOURCE-DOC GAP: the two named design sources (docs/architecture-variant-b.md, docs/yjs-collab-guide.md) do not exist and the rewrite spec never mentions realtime/Yjs, so the entire feature design is unspecified" -> Proceed from substrate + feature line: Proceed, but constrain the derivation to the single architecture the verified reality actually supports (do not treat "all specifics open" as license to invent infra that isn't there):

TRANSPORT/AUTH: One WS route on the existing uvicorn[standard] process, mounted under /api/v1 as a new router module (apps/api/app/api/router.py). Browser WS can't send Authorization, so pass the existing HS256 JWT via Sec-WebSocket-Protocol (or first-message), re-validate with decode_access_token + email->User lookup exactly as get_current_user (apps/api/app/core/security.py, apps/api/app/api/deps.py). Add the WS origin to CORS_ORIGINS and to apps/web/src/shared/config/env.ts.

AUTHORITY/DURABILITY (the hard constraint): single process, no Redis/broker, spins down when idle — so the in-process Y.Doc-per-textBox is the room authority for the free tier, but it MUST be backed by DB snapshotting to survive restart/spindown. Add an additive Alembic revision on top of head 0003 introducing a CRDT-state column/table (follow camelCase `textBox` naming; e.g. store the Yjs update blob) so a reconnecting/cold client rehydrates from Postgres. This satisfies F3/F5 within the stated infra; it does NOT give multi-node fan-out (single process only).

MATERIALIZATION & SIDE EFFECTS (F5): the async collab persistence loop cannot reuse the sync get_db (apps/api/app/db/session.py) — use its own threadpool/session. Write-back MUST go through the ORM (or explicitly set server_default/onupdate timestamps) or "last edited" freezes, and MUST re-hook _notify_new_mentions / mention-diffing that currently live only in the REST PATCH path (apps/api/app/api/routes/records.py) or mentions silently stop firing. Reconcile the CRDT text with the whole-string-replace REST semantics of textBox_content (String(1000)).

AUTHZ/UI: every collab mutation enforces require_project_editor via textBox->record->project_id (apps/api/app/api/project_access.py); viewers get read-only presence. Presence/awareness reuses the already-serialized ProjectRead.members roster in apps/web/src/features/records/stores/records.store.ts; identity stays JWT user_id/email, not CRDT clientID. Client code lands in the records feature slice reusing shared/api/client.ts's token pattern.

Scope stays textBox content only; projects/records/tags/memberships/notifications remain REST.
revisions.rationale: Verified: the two named sources (docs/architecture-variant-b.md, docs/yjs-collab-guide.md) are absent from the working tree, all branches, and the full `git log --all` history — and docs/architecture-variant-a.md, cited as evidence in a reality contract, is also absent. The only design doc is docs/specs/bricks-rewrite-spec.md, which never mentions realtime/Yjs/CRDT/WebSocket. GAP-locate is therefore not actionable: there is nothing to recover, and this READ-ONLY design task has no human channel to source the missing product decisions, so "author them first" merely relabels the same derivation as a documentation prerequisite while blocking all progress. Meanwhile the design is NOT actually unconstrained: the code-grounded reality contracts (all independently verified against real files) plus invariants F1–F5 already pin the architecture tightly — single-process free-tier authority with DB snapshotting, JWT-over-subprotocol WS auth reusing decode_access_token + project_access edit-gating, additive Alembic revision preserving camelCase `textBox` naming, ORM-driven write-back so updated_at/mentions/notifications re-fire, textBox-content-only scope. That is enough to produce a concrete, buildable design skeleton now. The option choice is decisive (resolved), but GAP-proceed legitimately surfaces one genuine human/product decision it cannot invent — see tradeoffForHuman.

revisions.change: Fork "Realtime transport / provider" -> WebSocket endpoint inside FastAPI (Starlette) + y-py: Adopt T-fastapi-ws, but implement the client against the STANDARD y-websocket wire protocol (sync step1/step2 + awareness), not a bespoke message format, and put the server's CRDT handling behind a thin provider seam. Concretely: (1) new Python WS router mounted under /api/v1 (add its origin to CORS_ORIGINS and VITE config), authenticating via JWT passed in the WS subprotocol or first message and re-validated with decode_access_token + get_project_access; viewers connect read-only. (2) Use pycrdt/y-py with pycrdt-websocket for the server side; store the encoded Y.Doc state in a new additive, camelCase-consistent snapshot column/table via a 0004 Alembic revision, rehydrated on first connect and snapshotted on debounce so state survives idle-spindown/restart. (3) On debounced convergence, write the flattened text back through the existing ORM update path (setting updated_at) and reuse _notify_new_mentions so mentions/notifications and 'last edited' keep firing; run this persistence work off the request DI via a dedicated sessionmaker in run_in_threadpool to respect the sync/async boundary. Because both this server and Hocuspocus speak the same y-websocket protocol, if the app ever outgrows a single process the server can be swapped to a Node Hocuspocus service (T-node) with essentially no frontend change — this de-risks the one assumption (single-node) that the choice rests on.
revisions.rationale: All four options presuppose a CRDT (Yjs family), so F1/F3/F4 are satisfiable by any of them; the real fork is WHERE the CRDT authority/relay lives and how it re-hooks the code's existing auth, persistence, and mention logic. Two facts decide it. (1) Production is a SINGLE uvicorn process with no workers/broker/Redis and no plan to scale horizontally (verified: entrypoint.sh runs `uvicorn app.main:app` bare; render.yaml free tier). So contract-#1's "in-process state does not fan out across nodes" concern is inert in the actual topology — every WS connection for a room lands on the one process. The residual real risk is durability across restart/idle-spindown, and the contract itself names DB snapshotting as an acceptable authority layer. (2) Auth, per-project edit gating (project_access, textBox→record→project_id), timestamp management (onupdate), and mention/notification creation ALL currently live inside one synchronous Python codebase. T-fastapi-ws keeps that logic in-process, so re-hooking it is a local change rather than a cross-service protocol.
